Read and write a frame's metadata as JSON

Source: R/metadata_json.R
metadata_json.Rd

get_metadata_json() gives a frame's metadata as JSON, which any language can read. set_metadata_json() restores metadata from that JSON, so that the round trip gives back exactly what get_metadata() gave.

This is how the metadata travels outside R, for instance in the key-value metadata of a Parquet file written by aniread.

Usage

get_metadata_json(data)

set_metadata_json(data, json)

Arguments

data

An aniframe. For set_metadata_json(), a frame of the class the metadata belongs to: its class decides which categories and slots are valid.

json

A JSON string from get_metadata_json(). Or that JSON already parsed with jsonlite::fromJSON(simplifyVector = FALSE), for when it is embedded in a larger document.

Value

get_metadata_json(): a JSON string. set_metadata_json(): data with the metadata from json.

Layout

The JSON has the categories of list_default_metadata() as objects, in the same order, with spec_version saying which version of the layout it follows:

  • A field with a fixed set of values (unit_time, unit_space, coordinate_system, ...) is its value as a string.

  • NA is null. source_sampling_rate can also be the string "NaN": a device with no fixed rate, which JSON has no number for.

  • start_datetime is an ISO 8601 time in UTC, to the microsecond, with its time zone beside it as start_timezone (an IANA name, or "" for the session's own).

  • axis_directions and axis_extents are objects from axis role to value.

  • In variables, each role is an object of slots. A slot that maps axis roles to columns (where$position) is an object; one that lists columns (what$keys) is an array, even with one column.

  • structure is an object of structures. Each has points (an array), segments and joints (arrays of row objects), and root, source, citation, license and variable.

Numbers are written with as few digits as read back exactly. Inf and -Inf, which JSON also has no number for, are strings like "NaN".

See also

get_metadata(), set_metadata()

Examples

x <- example_anipoint(n_obs = 2, n_individuals = 1)
json <- get_metadata_json(x)
json
#> [1] "{\"spec_version\":{\"aniframe\":\"3.0.0\",\"anievent\":\"1.0.0\"},\"recording\":{\"source\":null,\"source_version\":null,\"source_format\":null,\"source_sampling_rate\":null,\"filename\":null},\"time\":{\"unit_time\":\"frame\",\"sampling_rate\":null,\"sampling_interval\":1,\"start_datetime\":null,\"start_timezone\":\"\"},\"space\":{\"coordinate_system\":\"cartesian_2d\",\"reference_frame\":\"allocentric\",\"handedness\":\"unknown\",\"axis_directions\":{},\"axis_extents\":{},\"unit_space\":\"px\",\"unit_angle\":\"rad\",\"euler_sequence\":null,\"euler_intrinsic\":null},\"variables\":{\"what\":{\"keys\":[\"individual\",\"keypoint\"]},\"when\":{\"index\":[\"time\"],\"keys\":[\"session\",\"trial\"]},\"where\":{\"position\":{\"x\":\"x\",\"y\":\"y\"}},\"event\":{\"state\":[],\"point\":[]}},\"structure\":{}}"

y <- set_metadata_json(x, json)
identical(get_metadata(y), get_metadata(x))
#> [1] TRUE
